author: hodge
title: A Commentary on the Epistle to the Romans, designed for students of the English Bible
edition: Philadelphia: Grigg & Elliot, 1835 (first edition); text from archive.org OCR

rights.worldwide: to confirm: death dates of every author and editor named (life + 70 years); Charles Hodge died in 1878

notes: The first edition of 1835, not the revised edition of 1864; the text is archive.org's OCR of a scan of the 1835 Grigg & Elliot printing (commentaryonepis0000char). Each chapter section prints Contents, Analysis, Commentary, Doctrines and Remarks; the entries are the Commentary, every paragraph of it in the order printed, in entries of up to about 350 words (a paragraph cut between entries is marked with ' ...'). Each of Hodge's verse marks ('(1)', '(3, 4)') opens an entry; the heading is his lemma, where it is short. The Contents, Analysis, Doctrines and Remarks, which are on a whole section rather than on a verse, are left out. Hodge prints Greek words in parentheses; the OCR turns them into noise, so each such parenthesis is left out and marked ' ... '. Editing otherwise limited to joining hyphenated line ends and dropping running heads, page numbers, footnotes and footnote marks; A few footnotes that the OCR runs into the text at a page turn are left where they fall, and a few garbled Greek words outside parentheses may remain. OCR misreadings are left as they are unless listed in library/corrections/hodge-romans.json. The Open Word Bible text has no Romans 16:25-27 (its pinned SBLGNT data lacks the doxology), so the commentary on those verses is not included until the verses are.
